knowledge_points.name: Perception
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Perception is the process of understanding and interpreting sensations.
knowledge_points.plain: 理解和解释感觉的过程

knowledge_points.name: Psychophysics
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Psychophysics is the study of the interaction between the sensations we receive and our experience of them.
knowledge_points.plain: 研究感觉与主观体验的关系

knowledge_points.name: absolute threshold
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The absolute threshold is the smallest amount of stimulus we can detect.
knowledge_points.plain: 能觉察到的最小刺激量

knowledge_points.name: subliminal
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Stimuli below our absolute threshold are said to be subliminal.
knowledge_points.plain: 低于绝对阈限的刺激

knowledge_points.name: difference threshold
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The difference threshold, sometimes called a just-noticeable difference, is the smallest amount of change needed in a stimulus before we detect a change.
knowledge_points.plain: 刚能觉察的刺激最小变化

knowledge_points.name: Weber’s law
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This threshold is computed by Weber’s law, which states that the change needed is proportional to the original intensity of the stimulus.
knowledge_points.plain: 变化量与原有刺激强度成正比

knowledge_points.name: signal detection theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Signal detection theory investigates the effects of the distractions and interference we experience while perceiving the world.
knowledge_points.plain: 研究干扰下如何觉察刺激

knowledge_points.name: false positive
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A false positive is when we think we perceive a stimulus that is not there.
knowledge_points.plain: 误以为存在实际没有的刺激

knowledge_points.name: false negative
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A false negative is not perceiving a stimulus that is present.
knowledge_points.plain: 未觉察到实际存在的刺激

knowledge_points.name: top-down processing
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Top-down processing occurs when you use your background knowledge to fill in gaps in what you perceive.
knowledge_points.plain: 用背景知识补全所感知信息

knowledge_points.name: schemata
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Our experience creates schemata (also called schema), which are mental representations of how we expect the world to be.
knowledge_points.plain: 对世界如何运作的心理表征

knowledge_points.name: perceptual set
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Schemata can create a perceptual set, which is a predisposition to perceiving something in a certain way.
knowledge_points.plain: 以特定方式感知事物的倾向

knowledge_points.name: bottom-up processing
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Instead of using our experience to perceive an object, we use only the features of the object itself to build a complete perception.
knowledge_points.plain: 依据刺激本身特征构建知觉

knowledge_points.name: figure-ground relationship
knowledge_points.definition_quote: One of the first perceptual decisions our mind must make is the figure-ground relationship. What part of a visual image is the figure and what part is the ground or background?
knowledge_points.plain: 区分图形与背景的知觉关系

knowledge_points.name: Gestalt psychology
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The Gestalt psychology points out that we normally perceive images as groups, not as isolated elements.
knowledge_points.plain: 强调整体组织而非孤立元素

knowledge_points.name: Proximity
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Objects that are close together are more likely to be perceived as belonging in the same group.
knowledge_points.plain: 邻近的物体易归为一组

knowledge_points.name: Similarity
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Objects that are similar in appearance are more likely to be perceived as belonging in the same group.
knowledge_points.plain: 相似的物体易归为一组

knowledge_points.name: Continuity
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Objects that are arranged in a continuous line or curve (such as a trail or a geometric figure) are more likely to be perceived as belonging in the same group.
knowledge_points.plain: 连续线条或曲线易归为一组

knowledge_points.name: Closure
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Objects that make up a recognizable image are more likely to be perceived as belonging in the same group even if the image contains gaps that the mind needs to fill in; note that this perception is influenced by top-down processing.
knowledge_points.plain: 补全缺口以看成完整图形

knowledge_points.name: constancy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Our ability to maintain a constant perception of an object despite these changes is called constancy.
knowledge_points.plain: 随条件变化仍保持知觉恒定

knowledge_points.name: size constancy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: We keep a constant size in mind for an object (if we are familiar with the typical size of the object) and know that it does not grow or shrink in size as it moves closer or farther away.
knowledge_points.plain: 随距离变化仍知物体大小不变

knowledge_points.name: shape constancy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Objects viewed from different angles produce different shapes on our retinas, but we know the shape of an object remains constant.
knowledge_points.plain: 视角变化仍知物体形状不变

knowledge_points.name: brightness constancy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: We perceive objects as being a constant color even as the light reflecting off the object changes.
knowledge_points.plain: 光照变化仍知物体颜色不变

knowledge_points.name: stroboscopic effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A common example of this is the stroboscopic effect, used in movies or flip books. Images in a series of still pictures presented at a certain speed will appear to be moving.
knowledge_points.plain: 连续静止画面看起来在运动

knowledge_points.name: phi phenomenon
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Another example you have probably encountered on movie marquees and with holiday lights is the phi phenomenon. A series of lightbulbs turned on and off at a particular rate will appear to be one moving light.
knowledge_points.plain: 灯光依次明灭看似一个光点在动

knowledge_points.name: autokinetic effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A third example is the autokinetic effect. If a spot of light is projected steadily onto the same place on a wall of an otherwise dark room and people are asked to stare at it, they will report seeing it move.
knowledge_points.plain: 暗室固定光点看似移动

knowledge_points.name: depth perception
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Without depth perception, we would perceive the world as a two-dimensional flat surface and be unable to differentiate between what is near and what is far.
knowledge_points.plain: 判断远近和三维空间的能力

knowledge_points.name: visual cliff
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Researcher Eleanor Gibson used the visual cliff experiment to determine when human infants can perceive depth. An infant is placed onto one side of a glass-topped table that creates the impression of a cliff.
knowledge_points.plain: 制造悬崖错觉的玻璃台实验

knowledge_points.name: monocular depth cues
knowledge_points.definition_quote: monocular depth cues (depth cues that do not depend on having two eyes)
knowledge_points.plain: 不需双眼参与的深度线索

knowledge_points.name: linear perspective
knowledge_points.definition_quote: One of the most common cues is linear perspective. If you wanted to draw a railroad track that runs away from the viewer off into the distance, most likely you would start by drawing two lines that converge somewhere toward the top of your paper.
knowledge_points.plain: 平行线汇聚表现纵深感

knowledge_points.name: relative size
knowledge_points.definition_quote: If you added a drawing of the train, you might use the relative size cue. You would draw the boxcars closer to the viewer as larger than the engine off in the distance.
knowledge_points.plain: 近大远小判断物体远近

knowledge_points.name: interposition
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A water tower blocking our view of part of the train would be seen as closer to us due to the interposition cue; objects that block the view to other objects must be closer to us.
knowledge_points.plain: 被遮挡物显得更远

knowledge_points.name: texture gradient
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This cue is called texture gradient; we know that we can see details in texture close to us but not far away.
knowledge_points.plain: 近处纹理清晰远处模糊

knowledge_points.name: shadowing
knowledge_points.definition_quote: By shading part of your picture, you can imply where the light source is and thus imply depth and position of objects.
knowledge_points.plain: 用阴影暗示光源和深度

knowledge_points.name: binocular depth cues
knowledge_points.definition_quote: binocular depth cues (cues that depend on having two eyes)
knowledge_points.plain: 依赖双眼的深度线索

knowledge_points.name: retinal disparity
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Each of our eyes will view an object from a slightly different angle. The brain receives both images. It knows that if the object is far away, the images will be similar, but the closer the object is, the more disparity there will be between the images coming from each eye.
knowledge_points.plain: 双眼图像差异提供深度信息

knowledge_points.name: convergence
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The other binocular depth cue is convergence. As an object gets closer to our face, our eyes must move toward each other to keep focused on the object.
knowledge_points.plain: 物体靠近时双眼向内会聚

knowledge_points.name: perceptual sets
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Cross- cultural research demonstrates that some basic perceptual sets are learned from our culture.
knowledge_points.plain: 部分知觉定势由文化习得

knowledge_points.name: Muller-Lyer illusion
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Line A should look longer even though both lines are actually the same length.
knowledge_points.plain: 等长线段看起来长度不同

knowledge_points.name: noncarpentered cultures
knowledge_points.definition_quote: People who come from noncarpentered cultures that do not often use right angles and corners in their building and architecture are not usually fooled by the Muller-Lyer illusion.
knowledge_points.plain: 不常用直角的建筑文化

knowledge_points.name: extrasensory perception (ESP)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: someone claiming to have “extrasensory perception” is claiming to perceive a sensation “outside” the senses discussed in Unit 1.
knowledge_points.plain: 声称感知感官之外的信息

knowledge_points.name: thinking and creativity
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Describing thinking and creativity is one of the most challenging areas in the science of psychology.
knowledge_points.plain: 思维与创造力难以描述定义

knowledge_points.name: concepts
knowledge_points.definition_quote: We each have cognitive rules we apply to stimuli from our environment that allow us to categorize and think about the objects, people, and ideas we encounter.
knowledge_points.plain: 用于归类思考的心理规则

knowledge_points.name: prototypes
knowledge_points.definition_quote: We may base our concepts on prototypes, or what we think is the most typical example of a particular concept.
knowledge_points.plain: 概念中最典型的例子

knowledge_points.name: images
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Another type of thought, images, are the mental pictures we create in our minds of the outside world.
knowledge_points.plain: 头脑中对外界形成的心理图像

knowledge_points.name: algorithm
knowledge_points.definition_quote: An algorithm is a rule that guarantees the right solution by using a formula or other foolproof method.
knowledge_points.plain: 保证正确解的公式化方法

knowledge_points.name: heuristic
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A heuristic is a rule of thumb—a strategy we can use to make a quick but not necessarily accurate judgment in a situation.
knowledge_points.plain: 快速但不一定准确的判断策略

knowledge_points.name: availability heuristic
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Judging a situation based on examples of similar situations that come to mind initially.
knowledge_points.plain: 依据易想起的例子判断

knowledge_points.name: representativeness heuristic
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Judging a situation based on how similar the aspects are to prototypes the person holds in his or her mind.
knowledge_points.plain: 依据与原型相似度判断

knowledge_points.name: overconfidence
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Overconfidence is our tendency to overestimate how accurate our judgments are.
knowledge_points.plain: 高估自己判断的准确性

knowledge_points.name: belief bias
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Belief bias occurs when we make illogical conclusions to confirm our preexisting beliefs.
knowledge_points.plain: 为维护原信念而错误推理

knowledge_points.name: belief perseverance
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Belief perseverance refers to our tendency to maintain a belief even after the evidence we used to form the belief is contradicted.
knowledge_points.plain: 证据被推翻后仍坚持信念

knowledge_points.name: gambler’s fallacy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Another example of a limitation of a heuristic is the gambler’s fallacy: this occurs when we believe that a certain event or outcome is more or less likely to occur because of how often it has recently occurred.
knowledge_points.plain: 误以为近期结果改变下次概率

knowledge_points.name: sunk-cost fallacy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The sunk-cost fallacy can also influence our thinking in negative ways. Sometimes we are unwilling to change a course of action because we spent a lot of effort and time trying to make that solution work, even when it becomes clear that the course of action is unlikely to solve the problem.
knowledge_points.plain: 因已投入而不愿改变方案

knowledge_points.name: mental set
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Mental set (also called rigidity) refers to the tendency to fall into established thought patterns.
knowledge_points.plain: 固守既有思路解决问题

knowledge_points.name: functional fixedness
knowledge_points.definition_quote: One specific example of rigidity is functional fixedness, the inability to see a new use for an object.
knowledge_points.plain: 看不到物体的新用途

knowledge_points.name: subgoals
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Studies show that good problem solvers identify subgoals, which are smaller and more manageable problems they need to solve in order to solve the whole problem.
knowledge_points.plain: 把总问题拆成的较小问题

knowledge_points.name: confirmation bias
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Another obstacle to successful problem-solving is confirmation bias. Many studies show that we tend to look for evidence that confirms our beliefs and ignore evidence that contradicts what we think is true.
knowledge_points.plain: 只找支持自身信念的证据

knowledge_points.name: framing
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Framing refers to the idea that the same information can be presented in different ways and the method of presentation can drastically change the way we view a problem or an issue.
knowledge_points.plain: 表述方式影响问题判断

knowledge_points.name: convergent thinking
knowledge_points.definition_quote: convergent thinking, which is thinking pointed toward one solution
knowledge_points.plain: 指向单一解决方案的思维

knowledge_points.name: divergent thinking
knowledge_points.definition_quote: divergent thinking, which is thinking that searches for multiple possible answers to a question.
knowledge_points.plain: 寻求多个可能答案的思维

knowledge_points.name: models, or explanations, of how memory works
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Several different models, or explanations, of how memory works have emerged from memory research.
knowledge_points.plain: 解释记忆运作的不同模型

knowledge_points.name: three-box/information-processing model
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The principal model of memory is the three-box model, also called the information-processing model or the multi-store model. This model proposes the three stages that information passes through before it is stored (see Figure 9.1).
knowledge_points.plain: 信息经三阶段存储的记忆模型

knowledge_points.name: sensory memory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The first stop for external events is sensory memory. It is a holding tank for incoming sensory information.
knowledge_points.plain: 暂存外来感觉信息的容器

knowledge_points.name: iconic memory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: less than a second for visual information (iconic memory)
knowledge_points.plain: 视觉信息的极短暂感觉记忆

knowledge_points.name: echoic memory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: three to four seconds for auditory information (echoic memory)
knowledge_points.plain: 听觉信息约持续数秒

knowledge_points.name: selective attention
knowledge_points.definition_quote: We encode what we are attending to or what is important to us.
knowledge_points.plain: 选择编码重要或关注的信息

knowledge_points.name: cocktail party effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: However, once a sensory message that you knew was important (like someone saying your name or hearing someone shout “Fire!”) entered sensory memory, you switched your attention to that message, and it was encoded into your short-term memory. (This phenomenon is called the cocktail party effect.)
knowledge_points.plain: 重要声音会吸引注意并被编码

knowledge_points.name: inattentional blindness
knowledge_points.definition_quote: We’ve all experienced inattentional blindness: when we fail to perceive something that was in our visual field (and that our eyes probably sensed) because we weren’t paying attention to it and were intensely focused on something else.
knowledge_points.plain: 专注时看不见视野内事物

knowledge_points.name: change blindness
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A closely related experience is change blindness: sometimes we do not observe an obvious change in our visual world because we are selectively attending to something else and do not perceive that an object or person changed.
knowledge_points.plain: 未注意到视觉场景的明显变化

knowledge_points.name: short-term memory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Everything you are thinking at the current moment is held in your short-term memory, and if you are trying to do something with that information, it’s in your working memory.
knowledge_points.plain: 当前正在思考的信息的暂时存储

knowledge_points.name: working memory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Working memory is your ability to manipulate items in your short-term memory.
knowledge_points.plain: 操作短时记忆内容的能力

knowledge_points.name: central executive
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The central executive—monitors incoming information and determines what other systems should be involved in processing the information.
knowledge_points.plain: 监控信息并分配加工系统

knowledge_points.name: visuospatial sketchpad
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The visuospatial sketchpad—deals with visual information; this is our “mind’s eye” that we use to visualize the world.
knowledge_points.plain: 处理视觉空间信息的心理画板

knowledge_points.name: auditory loop
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The auditory loop—deals with words or numbers.
knowledge_points.plain: 处理词语或数字的语音回路

knowledge_points.name: maintenance rehearsal
knowledge_points.definition_quote: When you get a confirmation code, you probably need to repeat it to yourself until you type it in; this is an example of maintenance rehearsal.
knowledge_points.plain: 通过重复把信息保持在短时记忆

knowledge_points.name: elaborative rehearsal
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Elaborative rehearsal is a type of effortful processing: it occurs when we focus on putting mental effort into encoding the meaning of a term, an event, a process, and so on.
knowledge_points.plain: 努力加工信息意义以助编码

knowledge_points.name: semantic memory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This is closely related to semantic memory, which involves memories related to the significance or meaning of information.
knowledge_points.plain: 关于信息意义的记忆

knowledge_points.name: long-term memory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Long-term memory is our permanent storage.
knowledge_points.plain: 永久保存信息的记忆系统

knowledge_points.name: episodic memory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Memories of specific events, stored in a sequential series of events.
knowledge_points.plain: 按顺序储存的具体事件记忆

knowledge_points.name: semantic memory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: General knowledge of the world, stored as facts, meanings, or categories rather than sequentially.
knowledge_points.plain: 储存事实意义和类别知识

knowledge_points.name: procedural memory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Memories of skills and how to perform them.
knowledge_points.plain: 关于技能如何操作的记忆

knowledge_points.name: explicit memories
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Explicit memories (also called declarative memories) are what we usually think of first. They are the conscious memories of facts or events we actively tried to remember.
knowledge_points.plain: 主动回忆事实或事件的意识记忆

knowledge_points.name: implicit memories
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Implicit memories (also called nondeclarative memories) are unintentional memories that we might not even realize we have.
knowledge_points.plain: 无意形成且未意识到的记忆

knowledge_points.name: prospective memory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Yet another type of memory is prospective memory, which is your memory for things you plan to do in the future.
knowledge_points.plain: 记住未来要做的事情

knowledge_points.name: eidetic memory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Luria and other researchers showed that these rare individuals seem to use very powerful and enduring visual images.
knowledge_points.plain: 极少数人具有的逼真持久视觉记忆

knowledge_points.name: levels of processing model
knowledge_points.definition_quote: An alternate way to think about memory is the levels of processing model. This theory explains why we remember what we do by examining how deeply the memory was processed or thought about.
knowledge_points.plain: 按加工深度解释记忆的模型

knowledge_points.name: shallowly encoded
knowledge_points.definition_quote: If you simply repeat a fact to yourself several times and then write it on your test as quickly as you can, you have only shallowly encoded that fact and you will forget it quickly.
knowledge_points.plain: 只机械重复而浅层加工

knowledge_points.name: deeply encoded
knowledge_points.definition_quote: However, if you study the context and research the reasons behind the fact, you have deeply encoded it and will likely recall it later.
knowledge_points.plain: 结合语境和意义深入加工

knowledge_points.name: long-term potentiation
knowledge_points.definition_quote: At the neurological level, researchers focus on a process called long-term potentiation. Studies show that neurons can strengthen connections between each other.
knowledge_points.plain: 重复激活增强神经元连接

knowledge_points.name: encoding
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Encoding is the process by which we put information into our memories, and it can be affected by many factors.
knowledge_points.plain: 把信息放入记忆的过程

knowledge_points.name: primacy effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The primacy effect predicts that we are more likely to recall items presented at the beginning of a list.
knowledge_points.plain: 更易记住列表开头项目

knowledge_points.name: recency effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The recency effect is demonstrated by our ability to recall the items at the end of a list.
knowledge_points.plain: 更易记住列表末尾项目

knowledge_points.name: serial position effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Together the primacy effect and recency effect demonstrate the serial position effect (also called the serial position curve). This effect is seen when recall of a list is affected by the order of items in a list.
knowledge_points.plain: 回忆受项目在列表中位置影响

knowledge_points.name: method of loci
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A well-known example is the method of loci. This method involves using imagery to associate the things you want to remember with various places.
knowledge_points.plain: 用地点意象关联待记内容

knowledge_points.name: spacing effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: One of the most robust findings in memory research is called the spacing effect. Research has consistently demonstrated the benefit of spacing studying out or using what is called distributed practice, as opposed to massed practice.
knowledge_points.plain: 分散学习优于集中学习

knowledge_points.name: chunking
knowledge_points.definition_quote: However, this limit can be expanded through a process called chunking. If you want to remember a grocery list with 15 items on it, you should chunk, or group, the items into no more than seven groups.
knowledge_points.plain: 把多个项目分组以便记忆

knowledge_points.name: mnemonic devices
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Most mnemonic devices, which are memory aids, are really examples of chunking.
knowledge_points.plain: 借分组等技巧辅助记忆

knowledge_points.name: hippocampus
knowledge_points.definition_quote: By studying patients with specific brain damage, we know that the hippocampus is important in encoding new memories.
knowledge_points.plain: 负责编码新记忆的脑结构

knowledge_points.name: anterograde amnesia
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Individuals with damage to the hippocampus might have anterograde amnesia (cannot encode new memories) but can recall events already in memory.
knowledge_points.plain: 无法形成新的记忆

knowledge_points.name: retrograde amnesia
knowledge_points.definition_quote: People with retrograde amnesia have a different problem; they are unable to remember information learned before a trauma to the brain.
knowledge_points.plain: 不能回忆创伤前经历

knowledge_points.name: cerebellum
knowledge_points.definition_quote: (Studies on animals indicate that procedural memories are stored in the cerebellum.)
knowledge_points.plain: 储存程序性记忆的脑结构

knowledge_points.name: retrieval
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The last step in any memory model is retrieval, or getting information out of memory so we can use it.
knowledge_points.plain: 从记忆中提取信息

knowledge_points.name: recognition
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Recognition is the process of matching a current event or fact with one already in memory (e.g., “Have I smelled this smell before?”).
knowledge_points.plain: 把当前刺激与记忆匹配

knowledge_points.name: recall
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Recall is retrieving a memory with an external cue (e.g., “What does my Aunt Beki’s perfume smell like?”).
knowledge_points.plain: 依外部线索提取记忆

knowledge_points.name: retrieval cues
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Both rely on retrieval cues, which are stimuli that help people retrieve memories.
knowledge_points.plain: 帮助提取记忆的刺激

knowledge_points.name: tip-of-the-tongue phenomenon
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This temporary inability to remember information is sometimes called the tip-of-the-tongue phenomenon.
knowledge_points.plain: 暂时想不起来但觉得知道

knowledge_points.name: semantic network theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: One theory that explains why this might work is the semantic network theory. This theory states that our brain might form new memories by connecting their meaning and context with meanings already in memory.
knowledge_points.plain: 记忆按语义相互连接成网

knowledge_points.name: flashbulb memories
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Also called flashbulb memories, these memories are powerful because the importance of the event caused us to encode the context surrounding the event.
knowledge_points.plain: 对重大事件的生动记忆

knowledge_points.name: mood-congruent memory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Studies consistently demonstrate the power of mood-congruent memory or the greater likelihood of recalling an item when our current mood matches the mood we were in when the event happened.
knowledge_points.plain: 情绪与记忆时相符更易提取

knowledge_points.name: state-dependent memory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: State-dependent memory refers to the phenomenon of recalling events encoded while in particular states of consciousness.
knowledge_points.plain: 在相同意识状态下更易提取

knowledge_points.name: constructed memory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A constructed memory (or reconstructed memory) includes false details of a real event or might even be a recollection of an event that never occurred.
knowledge_points.plain: 含虚假细节或虚构事件的记忆

knowledge_points.name: misinformation effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Studies show that leading questions (questions or statements that purposefully include information or events that never happened—called the misinformation effect) can easily influence us to recall false details, and questioners can create an entirely new memory by repeatedly asking insistent questions.
knowledge_points.plain: 误导信息改变错误记忆细节

knowledge_points.name: decay
knowledge_points.definition_quote: One cause of forgetting is decay: forgetting because we do not use a memory or connections to a memory for a long period of time.
knowledge_points.plain: 长期不用导致记忆消退

knowledge_points.name: relearning effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: If you have to memorize the capitals again, it will take you less time than it did the first time you studied them.
knowledge_points.plain: 重学遗忘内容用时更少

knowledge_points.name: interference
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Another factor that causes forgetting is interference. Sometimes other information in your memory competes with what you are trying to recall.
knowledge_points.plain: 其他记忆干扰目标记忆提取

knowledge_points.name: retroactive interference
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Learning new information interferes with the recall of older information.
knowledge_points.plain: 新学信息干扰旧信息提取

knowledge_points.name: proactive interference
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Older information learned previously interferes with the recall of information learned more recently.
knowledge_points.plain: 旧信息干扰新信息提取

knowledge_points.name: intelligence
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Francis Galton was a pioneer in the study of human intelligence and testing.
knowledge_points.plain: 高尔顿开创的智力研究领域

knowledge_points.name: psychometricians
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Although most teachers are experienced with creating tests, psychometricians are psychologists who specialize in making standardized tests.
knowledge_points.plain: 专门编制标准化测验的心理学家

knowledge_points.name: standardized test
knowledge_points.definition_quote: When we say that a test is standardized, we mean that the test items have been piloted on a similar population of people as those who are meant to take the test (the standardization sample) and that achievement norms have been established.
knowledge_points.plain: 经样本试测并建立常模的测验

knowledge_points.name: reliability
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Reliability refers to the repeatability or consistency of the test as a means of measurement.
knowledge_points.plain: 测验结果的一致性或可重复性

knowledge_points.name: split-half reliability
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Split-half reliability involves randomly dividing a test into two different sections and then correlating people’s performances on the two halves.
knowledge_points.plain: 两个半份测验分数相关

knowledge_points.name: equivalent-form reliability
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The correlation between performance on the different forms of the test is known as equivalent-form reliability.
knowledge_points.plain: 不同等值版本分数相关

knowledge_points.name: test-retest reliability
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Finally, test-retest reliability refers to the correlation between a person’s score on one administration of the test with the same person’s score on a subsequent administration of the test.
knowledge_points.plain: 同一测验前后两次分数相关

knowledge_points.name: validity
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A test is valid when it measures what it is supposed to measure.
knowledge_points.plain: 测验测量到目标特质的程度

knowledge_points.name: face validity
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Face validity refers to a superficial measure of accuracy.
knowledge_points.plain: 表面上看是否测量了目标

knowledge_points.name: content validity
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Content validity refers to how well a measure reflects the entire range of material it is supposed to be testing.
knowledge_points.plain: 覆盖应测内容全范围的程度

knowledge_points.name: concurrent validity
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Concurrent validity measures how much of a characteristic a person has now.
knowledge_points.plain: 测量个体当前具有的特质

knowledge_points.name: predictive validity
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Predictive validity is a measure of future performance.
knowledge_points.plain: 预测未来表现的能力

knowledge_points.name: aptitude tests
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Aptitude tests measure ability or potential
knowledge_points.plain: 测量能力或潜力的测验

knowledge_points.name: achievement tests
knowledge_points.definition_quote: achievement tests measure what one has learned or accomplished
knowledge_points.plain: 测量已学知识或成就的测验

knowledge_points.name: speed tests
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Speed tests generally consist of a large number of questions asked in a short amount of time.
knowledge_points.plain: 限时完成大量题目的测验

knowledge_points.name: power tests
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The goal of a power test is to gauge the difficulty level of problems an individual can solve.
knowledge_points.plain: 测量能解决多难问题的测验

knowledge_points.name: group tests
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Group tests are administered to many people at a time.
knowledge_points.plain: 同时施测许多人的测验

knowledge_points.name: individual tests
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Individual tests involve greater interaction between the examiner and the examinee.
knowledge_points.plain: 需考官与受测者互动

knowledge_points.name: intelligence
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Typically, intelligence is defined as the ability to gather and use information in productive ways.
knowledge_points.plain: 收集并有效运用信息的能力

knowledge_points.name: g
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Intelligence can be measured by a single, general ability (g).
knowledge_points.plain: 斯皮尔曼提出的单一一般智力

knowledge_points.name: factor analysis
knowledge_points.definition_quote: factor analysis, which is a statistical technique that measures the correlations between different items
knowledge_points.plain: 测量项目间相关性的统计方法

knowledge_points.name: multiple intelligences
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Theory of multiple intelligences—the term “intelligence” should be applied to a wide variety of abilities including kinesthetic, musical, interpersonal, intrapersonal, naturalistic, verbal, spatial, and mathematical.
knowledge_points.plain: 认为智力包含多种能力

knowledge_points.name: intrapersonal intelligence
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Intrapersonal intelligence refers to one’s ability to understand oneself.
knowledge_points.plain: 理解自己内心世界的能力

knowledge_points.name: interpersonal intelligence
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Interpersonal intelligence, on the other hand, corresponds to a person’s ability to get along with and be sensitive to others.
knowledge_points.plain: 与他人相处并理解他人的能力

knowledge_points.name: naturalist intelligence
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Finally, naturalist intelligence is found in people gifted at recognizing and organizing the things they encounter in the natural environment.
knowledge_points.plain: 识别并组织自然事物的能力

knowledge_points.name: triarchic theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Triarchic theory of intelligence—people can be intelligent in different ways; they can evidence analytic, practical, and creative intelligence.
knowledge_points.plain: 智力可分为分析实践创造三类

knowledge_points.name: Componential, or analytic, intelligence
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Componential, or analytic, intelligence involves the skills traditionally thought of as reflecting intelligence.
knowledge_points.plain: 传统智力测验所反映的能力

knowledge_points.name: creative intelligence
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The second type, experiential or creative intelligence, focuses on people’s ability to use their knowledge and experiences in new and innovative ways.
knowledge_points.plain: 用知识经验创新解决问题的能力

knowledge_points.name: practical intelligence
knowledge_points.definition_quote: People with this type of intelligence are what we consider street-smart
knowledge_points.plain: 把知识用于现实情境的能力

knowledge_points.name: fluid intelligence
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Fluid intelligence refers to our ability to solve abstract problems and pick up new information and skills, while crystallized intelligence involves using knowledge accumulated over time.
knowledge_points.plain: 解决抽象问题并学习新技能

knowledge_points.name: crystallized intelligence
knowledge_points.definition_quote: crystallized intelligence involves using knowledge accumulated over time.
knowledge_points.plain: 运用长期积累的知识

knowledge_points.name: EQ
knowledge_points.definition_quote: EQ roughly corresponds to Gardner’s notions of interpersonal and intrapersonal intelligence.
knowledge_points.plain: 对应人际与内省智力的情商

knowledge_points.name: mental age
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Binet came up with the concept of mental age, an idea that presupposes that intelligence increases as one gets older.
knowledge_points.plain: 与生理年龄对应的智力年龄

knowledge_points.name: IQ
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A person’s IQ score on this test is computed by dividing the person’s mental age by his or her chronological age and multiplying by 100.
knowledge_points.plain: 心理年龄除以实际年龄乘一百

knowledge_points.name: deviation IQ
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The Wechsler tests yield IQ scores based on what is known as deviation IQ. The tests are standardized so that the mean is 100, the standard deviation is 15, and the scores form a normal distribution.
knowledge_points.plain: 按标准差偏离均值计算智商

knowledge_points.name: Wechsler Adult Intelligence Scale (WAIS)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The Wechsler Adult Intelligence Scale (WAIS) is used in testing adults
knowledge_points.plain: 用于成人的韦氏智力测验

knowledge_points.name: Bias in testing
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Interestingly, researchers seem to agree that although different races and genders may score differently on these tests, the tests have the same predictive validity for all groups.
knowledge_points.plain: 测验是否公平对待不同群体

knowledge_points.name: nature
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Keep in mind that nature refers to the influence of genetics, while nurture stresses the importance of the environment and learning.
knowledge_points.plain: 遗传对特质的影响

knowledge_points.name: nurture
knowledge_points.definition_quote: nurture stresses the importance of the environment and learning.
knowledge_points.plain: 环境与学习的影响

knowledge_points.name: heritability
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Heritability is a measure of how much of a trait’s variation is explained by genetic factors.
knowledge_points.plain: 遗传因素解释特质变异的比例

knowledge_points.name: Flynn effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Performance on intelligence tests has been increasing steadily throughout the century, a finding known as the Flynn effect.
knowledge_points.plain: 智力测验成绩随年代持续上升

knowledge_points.name: Monozygotic (identical) twins
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Monozygotic (identical) twins, who share 100 percent of their genetic material, score much more similarly on intelligence tests than do dizygotic (fraternal) twins, who have, on average, only 50 percent of their genes in common.
knowledge_points.plain: 同卵双胞胎智力分数更相似

knowledge_points.name: Head Start
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Participation in government programs such as Head Start, meant to redress some of the disadvantages faced by impoverished groups, has been shown to correlate with higher scores on intelligence tests.
knowledge_points.plain: 帮助贫困儿童的政府早期项目

knowledge_points.name: differences within groups
knowledge_points.definition_quote: After putting the issue of cause aside, when comparing groups of people on any characteristic, keep in mind that differences within groups generally dwarf differences between groups.
knowledge_points.plain: 组内差异通常大于组间差异

knowledge_points.name: A CAUTIONARY NOTE
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Thus, we need to take care not to ascribe too great a meaning to a test score.
knowledge_points.plain: 不宜过度解读测验分数
